_about: The parameter experiments run with the formulation-3 MILP (code/solve_milp_f3.py) and RL1 (RL1_reinforcement_learning_method_1). Each experiment changes ONE factor at a time; every other input stays as in the baseline run (new_results = MILP milp_300s, RL1 results = rl1). The baseline value is NOT solved again: the analysis takes it from those two folders. Experiment numbers are those of the experiment table (1-8); priority 1 runs first. Paths are relative to the project folder (the parent of comparative_results).

instances._about: Same instance set as the baseline runs: the 56 Solomon files (CSV source 'solomon', 100 EVs each) at n = 10, 20, ..., 100 = 560 instances. An experiment may restrict the Solomon families (E3).

baseline._about: Folders and run ids of the finished baseline runs (results_io layout).

solver._about: Settings of the experiment runs. They equal the baseline runs (300 s, 8 workers x 4 threads, Gurobi seed 0, greedy warm start; RL1 model_best.pt, 8 symmetries x (1 + 64) rollouts), so a variant differs from the baseline only in its input.

experiments.name: Value of charging time at theta = 1, c^{C,1}
experiments.question: How sensitive is the van share to the most influential assumed value?

experiments.name: Money sensitivity at theta = 0, mu^0
experiments.question: How sensitive are Z and the van share to the coefficient with the largest elasticity on Z?

experiments.name: Van tariff p^M
experiments.question: Who gets vans, and at what cost to the operator and equity?

experiments.name: Van fleet and seats (one at a time)
experiments.question: Where does another van or seat pay off, and where is capacity idle?

experiments.name: Van battery upper bound B
experiments.question: Is recharging worth modelling? If Z barely moves, drop it.

experiments.name: Guns per station
experiments.question: Do guns fix peak queues, and who benefits?

experiments.name: Income distribution
experiments.question: Does the van share follow the Table 25 estimate (Beta reweighting) once re-solved?
experiments._about: theta is re-drawn by quantile mapping: theta_new = F_new^-1(F_Beta(2,2)(theta_base)), so every EV keeps its income rank (the richest EV stays the richest) and only the shape of the distribution changes.

experiments.name: Horizon T (R1 and RC1 only)
experiments.question: How much does the deadline cost, and how many infeasible instances become feasible?
experiments._about: Priority 5 = optional: not in default_priorities (the classes with a long horizon, C2 / R2 / RC2, already show the horizon effect). Run it with --priority 5 or --experiments E3. T is multiplied by the factor for the R1 and RC1 files only, and only those 20 files (200 instances) are solved.
